question: Can faster exact SHA-256 and bounded overlap reduce first-open full EMPAD residency without changing source identity, counts, or memory policy?

parameters.initial_probe: CryptoKit/CommonCrypto/CryptoKit SHA-256 of the complete original file; 32 MiB read window; three repetitions each

followup_probe: Compare 512/256/512-frame pipelined windows. Halving a window may recover the extra transient 32 MiB staging without sacrificing overlap; resident count bytes must remain identical.

outputs.result: Native full first-open 2.11-2.39 to 1.53-1.61 seconds, exact billion-word parity, same resident bytes, bounded peak. One-second first-open target unmet; folder-return cancellation fixed and retested. No release or FPS claim.
